name: Apache Airflow
manual_override_reason: the automated pick (airbyte) has to be excluded: its own root LICENSE file is genuinely Elastic License 2.0 (verified via a fresh clone, matching this pipeline's own acquire.py classifier output), a source-available licence that is explicitly refused by this pipeline's own licence policy (restricts who can run the software), not open source. No fallback candidate was listed for this category slot. A first substitute, Meltano (MIT, verified via fresh clone), was investigated and rejected: Meltano dropped its web UI entirely as of v2/v3 and is now CLI-only ('Meltano will eventually have a UI again...' per its own troubleshooting docs), incompatible with this pipeline's browser-screen-verification requirement. Substituted Apache Airflow instead (Apache-2.0, verified via fresh clone) - the single most canonical open-source data-engineering/workflow-orchestration tool, with a full, rich web UI, and already a valid-licence candidate this same pipeline's own discovery step surfaced for the neighbouring 'automation' category (APP-009). This mirrors the existing substitution precedent in this repo (APP-038: Pi-hole -> Uptime Kuma, same reason - bad licence on the automated pick).

install_startup.recipe_modification_note: The repo's own officially-documented production quick-start (airflow-core/docs/howto/docker-compose/docker-compose.yaml) is a full CeleryExecutor cluster (postgres + redis + api-server + scheduler + dag-processor + celery worker + triggerer + init container) built for a real multi-node deployment, not a lightweight local trial. Used the project's own OTHER officially-documented quick-start instead: `airflow standalone` (see airflow's own CLI --help: 'Run an all-in-one copy of Airflow'), a single container that runs the api-server, scheduler, triggerer and dag-processor together against a bundled SQLite database - the exact command Airflow's own Quick Start guide recommends for trying the app out. Pulled apache/airflow (no version-pinned tag was resolvable against this checkout's own in-development __version__; used the ':latest' tag via Google's public Docker Hub mirror per the same sandbox-wide CDN workaround as APP-003/APP-005/APP-009, then retagged locally to the real released version its own OCI label reports it corresponds to, 3.3.2) and ran it with AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES=true so there is real, non-empty content (116 example DAGs) to browse and exercise. `airflow standalone` generates a random admin password on first boot and prints it to the container's own logs rather than using a fixed default - read fresh from `docker logs` by both the screen-walk and capability scripts rather than hardcoded.

screen_summary.verification_note: Driven by a tailored Playwright script (airflow_walk.py) rather than the generic screens.py crawler, since the generic crawler's fixed test credentials (libwalker/Walker-Pass-2026!) can never log in to a `standalone`-mode instance, whose single admin account and RANDOM password only exist inside the container's own logs. Real admin login, then 16/16 real screens reached, rendered, and browser-verified: the Welcome/Home dashboard, the DAGs list (116 real example DAGs), a specific DAG's Grid/Runs/Tasks/Code/Details tabs, Assets, Browse > DAG Runs + Task Instances, and Admin > Connections/Variables/Pools + Security > Permissions + Config.

capability_summary.verification_note: Driven by a tailored script (airflow_capabilities.py), independent reconfirmation for each. (1) DAG Trigger: manually triggered a real run of the example_bash_operator DAG via the UI's own Trigger button, confirmed not from the browser session that triggered it but from the scheduler's own database, queried fresh via `airflow dags list-runs` inside the container (the single most authoritative source available for this fact) - a genuine new DagRun with state 'success' was created and ran to completion; real attach point at airflow-core/src/airflow/api/common/trigger_dag.py's trigger_dag. (2) Admin - Variables: created a real Variable with a unique key/value via the Admin > Variables form, independently reconfirmed listed by key from a brand-new browser context with a fresh login; real attach point at airflow-core/src/airflow/models/variable.py's Variable model.
